SMTO-EXE-0062 — The window SMTO was waiting for didn't appear in time

GUID: d1183fa1-af90-5fa6-978d-0c9e0315e117
Slug: desktop-timeout
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • SMTO waited for a window to show up on the Gateway computer, but none matching what it was looking for appeared before time ran out. The app may still be opening.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the screen of the computer the Gateway runs on (the Gateway is the helper program SMTO uses there). See whether the app opened, is still loading, or shows a pop-up. SMTO stops waiting after a few seconds unless told otherwise, so a slow app may simply still be starting.
  2. In the conversation, ask SMTO to list the open windows on that computer. Don't ask it to open the app again yet. The list shows each window's real title and app, and opening the app again could start a second copy.
  3. Ask SMTO to wait again using the exact window title or app name from that list, and to wait up to 30 seconds if the app is slow. A wait only succeeds when a window matches the details SMTO was told to look for, and 30 seconds is the longest it can wait.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the window it found, and only one copy of the app is open on the Gateway computer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name of the app you expected, to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't keep asking SMTO to open the app again; each request can start another copy.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway Desktop wait_for_window operation reached its timeout without any listed window matching the requested match criteria.

What this means

  • The bounded wait_for_window loop reached its deadline without observing a window matching the submitted structured criteria. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • The bounded wait_for_window loop reached its deadline without observing a window matching the submitted structured criteria.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect current windows and the exact match criteria, together with any original launch receipt.

How to fix it

  • List current windows and applications on the same Gateway, correct the match criteria (title, application_id or pid) and, for slow apps, raise timeout_seconds (default 5, maximum 30). The timeout does not prove the app never started, so check for an existing instance before issuing another launch_application.
  • Inspect current state and adjust the structured match before requesting another bounded wait.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect current state and adjust the structured match before requesting another bounded wait.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended window is observed with valid criteria or the unmet wait condition is reported without duplicate launch.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
